data.title: The Egyptian Book of the Dead
data.translator: Peter Le Page Renouf and Édouard Naville
data.license: Public domain in the United States
data.notes: Chapter and paragraph (BD 125.3): the chapter numbers are Lepsius's, as printed; the paragraphs are numbered in order. A chapter with a letter (30A, 30B) shares the number of its chapter. Renouf translated chapters 1 to 139, Naville 140 to 186. The chapters that are only a picture, a repeat of another chapter, or the editor's description have no passages.

data.title: The Poetic Edda
data.license: Public domain in the United States

data.title: The Prose Edda

data.notes: Part, chapter, and paragraph (Gylfaginning 34.2): the chapters are Brodeur's, and their paragraphs are numbered in order, with each verse in the paragraph before it. Gylfaginning 34 is the whole chapter. Brodeur's introduction and notes are not here; his brackets are kept.

data.title: Kojiki: Records of Ancient Matters
data.license: Public domain in the United States
data.notes: Section and paragraph (Kojiki 4.2): the 180 sections are Chamberlain's, and their paragraphs are numbered in order, with each song in the paragraph that leads into it. The passages that he gave in Latin are kept so. His introduction and notes are not here.

data.title: The Upanishads, Part 1
data.license: Public domain in the United States
data.notes: The three Upanishads of Sacred Books of the East 1 that are on Wikisource: the Khândogya, by book and Khanda (Khandogya 6.8, one passage for each Khanda, with Müller's verse numbers); the Kena or Talavakâra, by Khanda and verse (Kena 1.3); and the Îsâ, by verse (Isa 6). The Aitareya and the Kaushîtaki of that volume are not on Wikisource, so they are not here.

data.title: The Shû King (Book of Documents)
data.license: Public domain in the United States
data.notes: Part, book, and paragraph (Shu 2.1.3).
